statements.text: “There is room to protect both rights — without compromising religious values.”

statements.text: “I’m grateful for my association and relationships in my life that helped me better understand the experiences of the LGBTQ community and who have been patient with a religious, conservative Utah boy who grew up in the ‘60s and took a little longer to develop the appropriate empathy than I would like to admit,”

statements.context: Same speech, on how his view of the LGBTQ community changed

statements.text: “I believe that the LGBTQ community is a critical part of the fabric of our country and our state. They're deserving of our unequivocal love and respect, and their contributions here in Utah are utterly invaluable.”

statements.text: “Look, I played in sports. Our kids played in sports. I want all young people to have the experience of playing in sports, every young person,”
statements.context: ABC 'This Week' interview, asked about trans athletes in women's sports (quoted via The Hill)

statements.text: “I want those sports to be safe, and I have confidence that local schools and local communities can make those decisions without the federal government making them for them.”
statements.context: Same interview, continuation after “And I want those sports to be fair,”

statements.text: Additionally, the Department’s recent rhetoric, including its proclamation that it is “aggressively pursuing” cases involving transgender youth competing in sports based on their gender identity, has shown that the Department is continuing to use OCR as an ideological arm of the Trump Administration rather than an enforcer of civil rights law.
statements.context: Letter Schiff led to the Department of Education on the Office for Civil Rights

statements.text: “As we celebrate the valuable contributions of LGBTQ+ Americans during Pride Month, we must acknowledge our government’s troubling history of discrimination against, and mistreatment of, servicemembers and civil servants in this community. I’m proud to join Senators Kaine and Baldwin in a resolution to acknowledge this troubling history, even as we continue to fight for full equality in the face of hatred and bigotry,”
statements.context: Release on resolution apologizing for discrimination against LGBT federal employees

statements.text: “Americans, including LGBTQ Americans, should have the freedom to start or expand a family without additional financial and systemic barriers that make it harder to afford reproductive health care services. This bill is crucial in correcting outdated tax laws in order to support LGBTQ individuals in family planning care,”
statements.context: Release introducing Equal Access to Reproductive Care Act
